name: Schizophrenia & Psychosis Action Alliance
description: Support, education, and advocacy for people living with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and psychosis.

sections.title: About S&PA Alliance
sections.text: The Schizophrenia & Psychosis Action Alliance (S&PA, formerly Schizophrenia and Related Disorders Alliance of America) is the only national nonprofit focused exclusively on improving the lives of people affected by schizophrenia and related psychotic disorders. Founded in 2009, S&PA provides peer support, education, and advocacy for individuals living with schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and psychosis, as well as their families. The organization emphasizes the importance of lived experience in shaping programs and policies.

sections.title: Support and Connection
sections.text: S&PA offers peer support groups where people living with schizophrenia and psychosis can connect with others who understand their experiences. Online support groups meet regularly via video conference, providing a safe space for sharing, encouragement, and practical coping strategies. The organization also provides family support resources, recognizing that psychotic disorders affect entire families. Connection with peers who have achieved stability and recovery provides hope and practical guidance.

sections.title: Education and Resources
sections.text: S&PA provides educational resources about schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, and other psychotic conditions. Materials cover topics including understanding symptoms, treatment options, medication management, navigating the mental health system, and recovery strategies. The organization offers webinars featuring experts and people with lived experience. Resources emphasize that recovery is possible—many people with schizophrenia lead fulfilling lives with proper treatment and support.

sections.title: Advocacy Efforts
sections.text: S&PA advocates for improved treatment, services, and policies affecting people with serious mental illness. Advocacy priorities include increasing access to evidence-based treatments like Coordinated Specialty Care for first-episode psychosis, improving community mental health services, reforming involuntary treatment laws, and ensuring housing and employment opportunities for people with psychotic disorders. The organization works to reduce stigma by amplifying the voices of people living successfully with these conditions.

sections.title: Getting Involved
sections.text: People affected by schizophrenia and psychosis can join support groups, share their stories, participate in advocacy efforts, and connect with a community that understands. S&PA welcomes individuals living with psychotic disorders, family members, mental health professionals, and allies. The organization's annual conference brings together advocates, clinicians, and researchers. By joining S&PA, you can help change the conversation about schizophrenia and ensure that people with these conditions receive the support and opportunities they deserve.
